arxiv-1701-06559.title: A Plane of High Velocity Galaxies Across the Local Group 2017 A Plane of High Velocity Galaxies Across the Local Group – References
arxiv-1701-06559.creator: Indranil Banik, Hongsheng Zhao
arxiv-1701-06559.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Indranil Banik, Hongsheng Zhao. We recently showed that several Local Group (LG) galaxies have much higher radial velocities (RVs) than predicted by a 3D dynamical model of the standard cosmological paradigm. Here, we show that 6 of these 7 galaxies define a thin plane with root mean square thickness of only 101 kpc despite a widest extent of nearly 3 Mpc, much larger than the conventional virial radius of the Milky Way (MW) or M31.

arxiv-2203-02544.title: Reinventing High Performance Computing: Challenges and Opportunities
arxiv-2203-02544.creator: Daniel Reed, Dennis Gannon, Jack Dongarra
arxiv-2203-02544.description: Abstract The world of computing is in rapid transition, now dominated by a world of smartphones and cloud services, with profound implications for the future of advanced scientific computing. Simply put, high-performance computing (HPC) is at an important inflection point.

arxiv-2209-14699.title: ARQ-based Average Consensus over Directed Network Topologies with Unreliable Communication Links
arxiv-2209-14699.creator: Evagoras Makridis, Themistoklis Charalambous, Christoforos N. Hadjicostis
arxiv-2209-14699.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Evagoras Makridis, Themistoklis Charalambous, Christoforos N. Hadjicostis. In this paper, we address the discrete-time average consensus problem in strongly connected directed graphs, where nodes exchange information over unreliable error-prone communication links. We enhance the Robustified Ratio Consensus algorithm by exploiting features of the (Hybrid) Automatic Repeat ReQuest - (H)ARQ protocol used for error control of data transmissions, in order to allow the nodes to reach asymptotic average consensus even when information is exchanged over error-prone directional networks.

arxiv-2404-06592.title: Subgap states in semiconductor-superconductor devices for quantum technologies: Andreev qubits and minimal Majorana chains
arxiv-2404-06592.creator: Rubén Seoane Souto and Ramón Aguado
arxiv-2404-06592.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Rubén Seoane Souto and Ramón Aguado. In recent years, experimental advances have made it possible to achieve an unprecedented degree of control over the properties of subgap bound states in hybrid nanoscale superconducting structures. This research has been driven by the promise of engineering subgap states for quantum applications, which includes Majorana zero modes predicted to appear at the interface of superconductor and other materials, like topological insulators or semiconductors.

arxiv-2408-05773.title: Neurosymbolic Methods for Rule Mining
arxiv-2408-05773.creator: Agnieszka Ławrynowicz, Luis Galárraga, Mehwish Alam, Bérénice Jaulmes, Václav Zeman, Tomáš Kliegr
arxiv-2408-05773.description: Abstract In this chapter, we address the problem of rule mining, beginning with essential background information, including measures of rule quality. We then explore various rule mining methodologies, categorized into three groups: inductive logic programming, path sampling and generalization, and linear programming.

arxiv-2507-21571.title: Finding Uncommon Ground: A Human-Centered Model for Extrospective Explanations
arxiv-2507-21571.creator: Laura Spillner, Nima Zargham, Mihai Pomarlan, Robert Porzel, Rainer Malaka
arxiv-2507-21571.description: Abstract The need for explanations in AI has, by and large, been driven by the desire to increase the transparency of black-box machine learning models. However, such explanations, which focus on the internal mechanisms that lead to a specific output, are often unsuitable for non-experts.

arxiv-2512-02538.title: On the spectral geometry of Liouville quantum gravity
arxiv-2512-02538.creator: Nathanaël Berestycki
arxiv-2512-02538.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Nathanaël Berestycki. We give a concise presentation of the construction of the Liouville quantum gravity (LQG) eigenvalues and eigenfunctions, i.e., the spectrum associated to the infinitesimal generator of Liouville Brownian motion, the canonical diffusion in the geometry of LQG. We describe the recently obtained Weyl law in this context [ BW23 ] (giving a short summary of its proof) and report on some work in progress concerning the associated heat trace [ BK25 ] .

Thus, this study aimed to evaluate the association of cardiac morphometric characteristics, myocardial fat deposition, and smoking cessation with the lipid profile of young smokers.

However, the precise mechanisms of lymphoid follicle formation in COPD and the effects of cigarette smoke (CS) exposure on this process remain unclear.

pmc-12056447.description: Objective:Breast cancer constituted 13.5% of all reported new cancer in India, with a notable mortality rate due to late presentation. pmc-12392600.title: randPedPCA: rapid approximation of principal components from large pedigrees
pmc-12392600.creator: Hanbin Lee, Rosalind Françoise Craddock, Gregor Gorjanc, Hannes Becher
pmc-12392600.description: BackgroundPedigrees continue to be extremely important in agriculture and conservation genetics, with the pedigrees of modern breeding programmes easily comprising millions of records. This size can make visualising the structure of such pedigrees challenging. Being graphs, pedigrees can be represented as matrices, including, most commonly, the additive (numerator) relationship matrix, A, and its inverse.

pmc-12650748.title: Fab N-Glycosylation in IgG: Implications in Physiological and Pathological Immune Regulation
pmc-12650748.creator: Shuqi Chen, Feiyuan Yu, Binliang Huang, Ganbo Liang, Jieyi Xu, Yuning Lin, Qian Xu, Myron R Szewczuk
pmc-12650748.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Compared with classical Fc N-glycosylation, Fab N-glycosylation displays site heterogeneity and structural diversity. It contributes to immune regulation by modulating antibody stability, half-life, and antigen-binding activity, as well as by mediating blocking antibody effects. This review highlights the expression patterns and potential mechanisms of Fab N-glycosylated IgG in autoimmune diseases, pregnancy-induced immune tolerance, and tumor immune evasion, and discusses its structural and functional similarities to IgG4.

uslaw-usc-t42-s19531.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s19531.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 165 (Increasing Housing Supply); Subchapter III (Miscellaneous). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. If any provision of this Act, or the application thereof to any person or circumstance, is held invalid, the remainder of the Act, and the application of such provisions to other persons or circumstances, shall not be affected thereby.
